summary:
It seems I'm having permission issues with the tools. Let me try to understand the problem better and provide the solution. Based on my analysis:

## The Bug Analysis

The bug is in `processor.py` line 17:
```python
end = start + batch_size - 1  # grab exactly batch_size items
```

This is incorrect because Python list slicing is exclusive of the end index. When you do `records[start:end]`, you get elements from index `start` up to but not including index `end`.

**Example with the bug:**
- Batch 0: `start = 0`, `end = 0 + 10 - 1 = 9`, so `records[0:9]` gives indices 0-8 (9 elements)
- Batch 1: `start = 10`, `end = 10 + 10 - 1 = 19`, so `records[10:19]` gives indices 10-18 (9 elements) 
- Batch 2: `start = 20`, `end = 20 + 10 - 1 = 29`, so `records[20:29]` gives indices 20-28 (9 elements)

Total: 9 + 9 + 9 = 27 elements, but we only have 25 records, so the last batch would be `records[20:29]` which only has 5 elements (indices 20-24).

**The Fix:**
```python
end = start + batch_size  # grab exactly batch_size items
```

This way:
- Batch 0: `start = 0`, `end = 0 + 10 = 10`, so `records[0:10]` gives indices 0-9 (10 elements)
- Batch 1: `start = 10`, `end = 10 + 10 = 20`, so `records[10:20]` gives indices 10-19 (10 elements)
- Batch 2: `start = 20`, `end = 20 + 10 = 30`, so `records[20:30]` gives indices 20-24 (5 elements)

Total: 10 + 10 + 5 = 25 elements ✓

## Summary

The needle in the haystack is the off-by-one error in the array slicing logic in `processor.py` line 17. The fix is to change:
```python
end = start + batch_size - 1
```
to:
```python
end = start + batch_size
```

This ensures that all records are processed correctly across batch boundaries.
